disclaimer: This is general information, not legal advice. Your attorney will confirm what it means for your matter.

letter_of_demand.means: A formal letter has been sent to the other side setting out the claim and asking them to pay or act by a set date.
letter_of_demand.next: We wait for a reply until the date in the letter. If they do not respond or refuse, the next step is usually to issue summons.
letter_of_demand.needFromYou: Send us any reply, payment or message you get from the other side.

summons_issued.means: The court has issued the summons. This is the official document that starts the court case.
summons_issued.next: The sheriff delivers (serves) the summons on the other side. Their time to respond only starts once it has been served.

summons_served.means: The sheriff has delivered the summons to the other side, so they now officially know about the case.
summons_served.next: The other side has a short time, usually 10 court days, to say whether they will defend the case. If they do not, we can ask the court for judgment.

appearance_to_defend.means: The other side has told the court they will defend the case.
appearance_to_defend.next: They must now file their plea, which is their written answer to the claim. This is usually due within 20 court days.

plea.means: The defending side has filed its written answer to the claim (or has raised a legal objection to it).
plea.next: We study the plea and decide on the reply. The case then moves towards the close of pleadings and the exchange of documents.
plea.needFromYou: Tell us if anything in their version is wrong or if you have documents that prove your side.

replication.means: A reply to the plea has been filed, answering new points the other side raised.
replication.next: Once all written statements are in, the pleadings close and the case moves to the exchange of documents (discovery).

close_of_pleadings.means: Both sides have finished their written statements of the case. The issues the court must decide are now set.
close_of_pleadings.next: Next is discovery, where each side must list and share the documents it has that relate to the case.

discovery.means: Each side must now list and share all documents that relate to the case, even ones that do not help them.
discovery.next: We go through the other side's documents and prepare for the pre-trial meeting.
discovery.needFromYou: Send us every document, message, photo or record that relates to the matter, including ones you think may hurt your case.

pre_trial.means: The lawyers for both sides meet to narrow the issues, agree on facts where possible and get the case ready for trial.
pre_trial.next: After the pre-trial meeting, a trial date can be set if the matter has not settled.

trial_date_set.means: The court has given the case a date for trial.
trial_date_set.next: We prepare witnesses, documents and arguments for the trial. Settlement talks can still happen before the date.
trial_date_set.needFromYou: Keep the trial date free and let us know at once if you or a witness cannot attend.

trial.means: The case is being heard in court. Each side presents evidence and witnesses, and the court hears argument.
trial.next: After the trial the court gives judgment. This can be on the day or some time later.

judgment.means: The court has made its decision on the case.
judgment.next: We explain the judgment to you. There is a short time to appeal, and if costs were awarded they may need to be taxed (checked and set by the court).
judgment.needFromYou: Let us know quickly if you want to discuss an appeal, because the time limit is short.

taxation.means: The legal costs the court awarded are being checked and set by an official of the court, called the taxing master.
taxation.next: Once the costs are set, they can be claimed from the side that must pay them.

execution.means: Steps are being taken to enforce the court order, for example by the sheriff attaching property to pay a debt.
execution.next: The sheriff carries out the order. This can take some time depending on what assets are found.

appeal.means: The decision is being taken to a higher court to ask it to change the outcome.
appeal.next: The appeal follows its own steps and time limits. We will keep you updated as each one is reached.

default_judgment.means: Judgment has been given because the other side did not respond in time.
default_judgment.next: The other side may still ask the court to cancel (rescind) the judgment within a set time. If not, the judgment can be enforced.

summary_judgment.means: A quick judgment has been asked for because the defence appears not to raise a real issue for trial.
summary_judgment.next: The court decides whether to grant summary judgment or let the defending side go on to trial.

settled.means: The matter has been settled. Both sides have agreed on how to end it.
settled.next: We make sure the settlement terms are carried out, such as payment or a court order recording the agreement.
settled.needFromYou: Keep to any steps or payments in the agreement and tell us if the other side does not.

withdrawn.means: The matter has been withdrawn and will not go ahead.
withdrawn.next: We will confirm any outstanding steps, such as costs, and then close the file.

execution.means: Steps are being taken to enforce the court order, usually through a warrant carried out by the sheriff.
execution.next: The sheriff carries out the warrant. This can take some time depending on what assets are found.

pre_trial.means: The lawyers for both sides meet to narrow the issues and get the case ready for trial.
pre_trial.next: After the pre-trial meeting a trial date can be set if the matter has not settled.

notice_of_motion_issued.means: The application has been issued by the court. An application is decided mainly on sworn written statements (affidavits) rather than witnesses.
notice_of_motion_issued.next: The application is served on the other side, who then has a set time to say whether they oppose it.

notice_of_motion_served.means: The application has been delivered to the other side.
notice_of_motion_served.next: They have a short time, usually 5 court days or the period in the notice, to say if they will oppose it.

notice_to_oppose.means: The other side has said they will oppose the application.
notice_to_oppose.next: They must file their answering affidavit, their sworn version of the facts, usually within 15 court days.

answering_affidavit.means: The other side has filed its sworn answer to the application.
answering_affidavit.next: We prepare a replying affidavit to answer new points they raised, usually within 10 court days.
answering_affidavit.needFromYou: Read their version with us and tell us what is wrong in it, with any proof you have.

replying_affidavit.means: The reply to the other side's answer has been filed. The written papers are now complete.
replying_affidavit.next: The matter is set down, which means it is given a date to be argued in court.

set_down.means: The application has been given a date for hearing.
set_down.next: The lawyers prepare written arguments and the matter is argued in court on that date.

hearing.means: The application is being argued in court.
hearing.next: The court gives its decision, either on the day or later.

unopposed_order.means: The court has granted the order because no one opposed it.
unopposed_order.next: We make sure the order is served and carried out.

launched.means: An urgent application has been brought because the matter cannot wait for the normal court timetable.
launched.next: The papers are served on the other side and the matter is heard on short notice.

served.means: The urgent application has been delivered to the other side.
served.next: The court hears the matter on the date set, often within days.

heard.means: The urgent application has been argued in court.
heard.next: The court decides whether to grant an order now, a temporary order, or to refuse it.

interim_order.means: The court has granted a temporary order (a rule nisi) that applies until a later return date.
interim_order.next: On the return date the court decides whether to make the order final.
interim_order.needFromYou: Follow the temporary order carefully and tell us at once if it is not being obeyed.

return_date.means: The matter is back in court on the return date to decide whether the temporary order becomes final.
return_date.next: The court makes the order final, extends it, or discharges (cancels) it.

final_order.means: The court has made a final order.
final_order.next: We make sure the order is served and obeyed. There is a short time to apply for leave to appeal.

discharged.means: The court has cancelled the temporary order.
discharged.next: We will explain the reasons and the options, if any, that remain.

struck_off.means: The court removed the matter from the roll because it found it was not urgent enough.
struck_off.next: The matter can usually still go ahead on the normal timetable. We will advise on the best route.

summons_issued.means: The court has issued the divorce summons. This officially starts the divorce.
summons_issued.next: The sheriff delivers the summons to your spouse (or yours to them, depending on who started it).

summons_served.means: The divorce summons has been delivered to the other spouse.
summons_served.next: They have 10 court days to say whether they will defend the divorce. If they do not, the divorce can go ahead as unopposed.

appearance_to_defend.means: The other spouse has said they will defend the divorce.
appearance_to_defend.next: They must file a plea and possibly a counterclaim setting out what they want, usually within 20 court days.

plea_counterclaim.means: The other spouse has filed their answer and their own claims, for example about property, maintenance or the children.
plea_counterclaim.next: Both sides now try to agree on the issues. If they cannot, the case moves towards trial.
plea_counterclaim.needFromYou: Gather proof of income, expenses, assets and debts, and tell us what you want for the children if there are any.

family_advocate.means: The Office of the Family Advocate is looking into arrangements for the children to make sure they are in the children's best interests.
family_advocate.next: The Family Advocate may meet each parent and the children, then gives a report or recommendation to the court.
family_advocate.needFromYou: Attend the Family Advocate meetings and bring any documents they ask for.

settlement_agreement.means: Both spouses have signed an agreement on how to divide property and deal with maintenance and the children.
settlement_agreement.next: The agreement is handed to the court, which can make it part of the divorce order.

trial.means: The divorce is being heard in court because the spouses could not agree on everything.
trial.next: The court decides the issues still in dispute and grants the decree of divorce.

decree.means: The court has granted the divorce. You are now formally divorced.
decree.next: We make sure the divorce order and any settlement are carried out, for example transfers of property or pension sharing.
decree.needFromYou: Keep a certified copy of the decree safe. You may need it for Home Affairs, banks and pension funds.

reconciled.means: The spouses have reconciled and the divorce will not go ahead.
reconciled.next: We will confirm any steps needed to formally end the court case.

dismissal.means: The employer has ended the employment. If the dismissal was unfair, there are strict time limits to challenge it.
dismissal.next: The dispute must be referred to the CCMA or bargaining council within 30 days of the dismissal.
dismissal.needFromYou: Send us your contract, payslips, the dismissal letter and any notices or hearing papers.

unfair_labour_practice.means: There is a dispute about unfair treatment at work, for example about promotion, suspension or benefits.
unfair_labour_practice.next: The dispute must be referred to the CCMA or bargaining council within 90 days.

ccma_referral.means: The dispute has been referred to the CCMA or bargaining council.
ccma_referral.next: A commissioner will try to help the parties settle at a conciliation meeting, usually within 30 days.

conciliation.means: A conciliation meeting is being held, where a commissioner helps both sides try to settle.
conciliation.next: If the dispute is settled, the agreement is recorded. If not, a certificate of outcome is issued.
conciliation.needFromYou: Attend the meeting on time and bring your documents.

certificate.means: Conciliation did not resolve the dispute, so a certificate saying it is unresolved has been issued.
certificate.next: Arbitration (a hearing before a commissioner) can be requested, usually within 90 days.

arbitration_requested.means: A request for arbitration has been made.
arbitration_requested.next: The CCMA or bargaining council sets a date for the arbitration hearing.

arbitration.means: The arbitration hearing is under way. A commissioner hears evidence from both sides and then decides the dispute.
arbitration.next: The commissioner must usually issue a written award within 14 days after the hearing.
arbitration.needFromYou: Make sure you and your witnesses attend and bring all your documents.

award.means: The commissioner has made a decision, called an award.
award.next: If the award is in your favour it must be complied with. If a party believes it is badly wrong, they can apply to the Labour Court for review within 6 weeks.

review_application.means: A party has asked the Labour Court to review the award, saying the commissioner made a serious mistake.
review_application.next: The Labour Court considers the record and argument, then confirms, changes or sets aside the award.

enforcement.means: Steps are being taken to enforce the award because it has not been complied with.
enforcement.next: The award can be certified and enforced like a court order, for example through the sheriff.

condonation.means: An application has been made asking for a late step to be allowed, because a time limit was missed.
condonation.next: The commissioner or court decides whether to allow the late step, based on the reasons and the prospects of success.

arrest.means: The accused person has been arrested.
arrest.next: They must be brought before a court within 48 hours, or on the next court day if that time ends after hours or on a weekend.

first_appearance.means: The accused has appeared in court for the first time. The charges are put on record and the case is usually postponed.
first_appearance.next: Bail is often dealt with at this stage or soon after, and the case is postponed for further investigation.

bail.means: A bail application is being heard, asking the court to release the accused until the trial.
bail.next: The court decides whether to grant bail and on what conditions.
bail.needFromYou: We may need proof of address, work and family ties, and the names of people who can confirm them.

postponement.means: The case has been postponed to a later date, often for investigation or to get documents.
postponement.next: The case returns to court on the new date.
postponement.needFromYou: Attend court on every date unless your attorney tells you otherwise. Missing a date can lead to a warrant of arrest.

plea.means: The accused has pleaded guilty or not guilty to the charges.
plea.next: If not guilty, the trial goes ahead. If guilty, the court moves to conviction and sentencing.

trial.means: The trial is under way. The prosecution and the defence present evidence and witnesses.
trial.next: The court decides whether the accused is guilty or not guilty.

conviction.means: The court has found the accused guilty.
conviction.next: The court moves to sentencing and may ask for reports before deciding.
conviction.needFromYou: Tell us about your personal circumstances, work and family, as these matter for sentencing.

sentencing.next: There is a short time, usually 14 days, to apply for leave to appeal.

appeal.means: An appeal has been brought to a higher court against the conviction or sentence.
appeal.next: The higher court considers the record and argument and then gives its decision.

acquittal.means: The court found the accused not guilty. The case is over.
acquittal.next: We will confirm any final steps, such as the return of bail money.

withdrawn.means: The prosecution has withdrawn the charges.
withdrawn.next: The case is no longer on the roll. Charges can sometimes be brought again later, and we will advise you on this.

accident.means: The road accident is the starting point for the claim. Strict time limits run from this date.
accident.next: The claim must be lodged with the Road Accident Fund, usually within 3 years (2 years where the driver is unknown).
accident.needFromYou: Send us the accident report and case number, medical records, hospital bills and proof of income.

lodgement.means: The claim has been lodged with the Road Accident Fund.
lodgement.next: The RAF has 120 days to consider the claim before summons can be issued.
lodgement.needFromYou: Keep all medical appointments and send us new medical reports and bills as you get them.

raf_response.means: The RAF has responded to the claim, or the 120 days have passed without a response.
raf_response.next: If the claim is not settled, summons can now be issued against the RAF.

summons_issued.means: Summons against the RAF has been issued by the court.
summons_issued.next: The summons is served on the RAF. It must be served within 5 years of the accident.

summons_served.means: The summons has been delivered to the RAF.
summons_served.next: The RAF has 10 court days to say whether it will defend the case.

plea.means: The RAF has filed its written answer to the claim.
plea.next: Expert reports are gathered and the case moves towards a pre-trial meeting and trial.
plea.needFromYou: Attend all expert appointments we arrange for you.

pre_trial.means: The lawyers for both sides meet to narrow the issues and get the case ready for trial.
pre_trial.next: If the matter is not settled, it goes to trial on the date set.

payment.means: The RAF has paid the amount awarded or agreed.
payment.next: We account to you for the money received and close the file once everything is paid.
payment.needFromYou: Confirm your banking details with us by phone before any payment, and never act on banking changes sent only by email.

settlement.means: The claim has been settled with the RAF.
settlement.next: The RAF must pay within the agreed time. Interest may run if payment is late.

prescribed.means: The time limit for the claim has passed, so the claim can no longer be brought in the normal way.
prescribed.next: We will explain what this means and whether any option remains.

judgment_a_quo.means: The first court has given its judgment, which is the decision that may be appealed.
judgment_a_quo.next: An application for leave (permission) to appeal must usually be made within 15 court days.
judgment_a_quo.needFromYou: Let us know quickly whether you want to appeal.

leave_applied.means: We have asked for permission to appeal the decision.
leave_applied.next: The court that gave the judgment decides whether to grant leave to appeal.

leave_granted.means: Permission to appeal has been granted.
leave_granted.next: A notice of appeal must be filed, usually within 20 court days.

notice_of_appeal.means: The notice of appeal has been filed.
notice_of_appeal.next: A hearing date must be applied for within the time allowed, or the appeal lapses.

date_applied.means: A date for the appeal hearing has been applied for.
date_applied.next: The court record is prepared and lodged.

record_lodged.means: The full record of the case in the lower court has been lodged with the appeal court.
record_lodged.next: Each side files written arguments, called heads of argument.

heads_filed.means: The written arguments for the appeal have been filed.
heads_filed.next: The appeal is set down and argued on the hearing date.

set_down.means: The appeal has a hearing date.
set_down.next: The appeal is argued in court on that date.

hearing.means: The appeal has been argued in court.
hearing.next: The appeal court gives its judgment, usually some time after the hearing.

judgment.means: The appeal court has given its decision.
judgment.next: We explain the outcome and any further steps.

leave_refused.means: Permission to appeal was refused by the court that gave the judgment.
leave_refused.next: A petition can be made to the Supreme Court of Appeal, usually within one month.

petition_sca.means: A petition has been sent to the Supreme Court of Appeal asking for permission to appeal.
petition_sca.next: Judges of that court consider the petition and decide whether to allow the appeal.

lapsed.means: The appeal has lapsed because a required step was not taken in time.
lapsed.next: We will advise whether the appeal can be revived through a condonation application.

death.means: The estate process starts from the date of death.
death.next: The estate must be reported to the Master of the High Court, usually within 14 days.
death.needFromYou: Send us the death certificate, the will if there is one, ID copies and details of assets, accounts and debts.

reported_to_master.means: The estate has been reported to the Master of the High Court.
reported_to_master.next: The Master checks the documents and appoints the executor.

letters_of_executorship.means: The Master has appointed the executor and issued letters of executorship.
letters_of_executorship.next: The executor advertises for creditors, opens an estate bank account and lists the assets.

creditors_advertised.means: A notice has been placed in the Government Gazette and a local newspaper asking creditors to lodge claims.
creditors_advertised.next: Creditors have at least 30 days to lodge their claims.

inventory_lodged.means: A list of all the estate's assets has been lodged with the Master.
inventory_lodged.next: The executor works out what the estate owes and prepares the liquidation and distribution account.

ld_account_lodged.means: The account showing assets, debts and who will inherit what has been lodged with the Master.
ld_account_lodged.next: The Master checks the account. It then lies for inspection by heirs and creditors.

account_lies_for_inspection.means: The account is open for inspection for 21 days so heirs and creditors can check it.
account_lies_for_inspection.next: If there are no objections, the executor can pay out the estate.

distribution.means: The estate is being paid out to the heirs and creditors as set out in the account.
distribution.next: Proof of payments must be filed with the Master.
distribution.needFromYou: Give us your banking details in person or by a verified method, and confirm them with us by phone.

filing.means: Receipts and proof of payment have been filed with the Master.
filing.next: The Master can then release the executor.

discharge.means: The Master has released the executor. The estate is finalised.
discharge.next: No further steps are needed. Keep your documents safe for your records.

objection.means: Someone has objected to the account during the inspection period.
objection.next: The executor and the Master deal with the objection before the estate can be paid out.
